findings.reason: a worker cannot satisfy both halves of the same gate, and whichever it picks either loses benchmark coverage §6 would delete or leaves a §10 migration the plan says belongs to another section.
findings.text: clause (1) requires "the batched labeller and every other caller outside reduced_newton.py, forward_operator.py and forward.py" to read through topology.read and book through current.book, but the sentence newly added to clause (2) says "Tests, scripts and benchmarks that call the fixed-design read are §6's to delete"; the resolved followup records about 44 test files and 76 benchmark and script files that reference the legacy read, and a file such as benchmarks/constraint_shape_receipt.py (calls profile.operator.read) is both a caller clause (1) orders migrated and a file clause (2) orders §6 to delete

findings.reason: §10's gate passes with the legacy read still live in five modules, and §6 then deletes that read out from under them, so the breakage surfaces a section later than the one that owns the migration.
findings.text: the section's account of the legacy read's consumers names the batched labeller's `operator.read`/`operator._fixed_design_read` calls, `forward.py`, `reduced_newton.py` and the operator's own methods, but at head five package modules outside the three excluded ones reach the fixed-design read through `ForwardFluxOperator.read` (forward_operator.py:3192 delegates to `_fixed_design_read`): constraint.py:1486, display_flux.py:246, flux_iteration.py:545 and :769, shape_inverse.py (about twelve call sites), and transport/coupled_window.py; clause (2)'s test names only `Topology.read_qualification` and `ForwardFluxOperator._fixed_design_read`, which those callers never touch

response_events.note: §10 clause 1 now scopes the migration to package modules (nova/) and names them; tests, scripts and benchmarks outside the package are §6's alone, deleted where they only exercised the fixed-design read and re-pointed otherwise.

done_when-1.note: §10 clause 1 now scopes the migration to package modules (nova/) and names them; tests, scripts and benchmarks outside the package are §6's alone, deleted where they only exercised the fixed-design read and re-pointed otherwise.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — tests/test_batched_labeller.py and tests/test_labeller_receipt.py exist at head, the followup f-cfs-legacy-read-migration resolves at plan.html:398, and the cited module and symbol names exist.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — clause (1) is unscoped, so it demands every test, script and benchmark caller migrate onto topology.read while the sentence added to clause (2) hands those same files to §6 for deletion.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §10 places no evidence in a scratchpad or node-local path; its receipts are the paired suite arms and the two named tests, which the run record keeps.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §10 introduces no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into a symbol or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the section's account of who calls the legacy read lists the labeller, reduced_newton.py, forward_operator.py and forward.py, but omits the five package modules that reach it through `ForwardFluxOperator.read`, and clause (2)'s caller test cannot see that route.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §10 carries one deliverable, the production path off the legacy read (migrate the labeller, delete the thin wrappers), closable on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10 declares `depends-on converged-forward-solve#s8`, and §2's read (`Topology.read`, topology.py:1428) and §5 (`solve.fixed_point`) it consumes are upstream of s8, so neither is an undeclared wait.
